description: Preventive maintenance is a sub-program under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to preserve and prolong the lifespan of national roads. This program is typically carried out on roads that are in fair to poor condition, with the primary objective of preventing and delaying further deterioration to a state where extensive rehabilitation is necessary. Preventive maintenance aims to prevent and delay the deterioration of national roads to a bad condition where ultimately rehabilitation is required, which typically involves Asphalt Overlay, Asphalt Overlay with Correction, and Concrete Reblocking.Asphalt Overlay is done on roads in fair condition. It involves the application of an additional layer of asphalt, that covers imperfections in existing asphalt or concrete. It is commonly applied to pavement that hasminor damage like light cracking, mild deterioration, or slightly sunken areas. The process of overlaying asphalt commonly includes a leveling out of the old asphalt pavement, ensuring a smooth, even surface on which to add additional layers.Asphalt Overlay with Correction is done on roads in poor condition. It involves the repair of short intermittent damaged sections before applying asphalt overlay. For concrete roads, the most common type of corrective maintenance is a combination of concrete pavement restoration (CPR) in terms of the replacement of intermittent shattered slabs and asphalt overlay.Concrete reblocking is done on national roads in poor condition which involves selective reblocking or replacement of intermittent shattered slabs in bad condition. process aims to improve the pavement's load-bearing capacity, reduce the risk of potholes, and enhance the pavement's durability and longevity.

The Rehabilitation, Reconstruction, and Upgrading of Damaged Paved National Roads is the sub-program aimed at restoring the national roads to an optimal condition. This sub-program under Asset Preservation Program targets national roads that are in poor condition and are no longer cost-effective to maintain.Upgrading from asphalt to concrete is also a part of this sub-program. This involves replacing the asphalt surface with a concrete one, which provides enhanced durability, resistance to heavy loads, and reduced maintenance costs.

The Rehabilitation and Reconstruction of National Roads with Slips, Slope Collapse, and Landslide is a sub-program under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to protect and secure national roads against the devastating effects of natural disasters, particularly landslides, erosion, and slope collapses. This sub-program is designed to enhance the engineering design of national roads to withstand the impact of severe storms and natural calamities in support of climate change adaptation.

The Construction, Upgrading, and Rehabilitation of Drainage along National Roads is a Sub-program under Asset Preservation Program aims to construct, improve, and rehabilitate drainage structures such as box culverts, pipe culverts, side drains, and lined canals along national roads to prevent flooding and water run-off on the road surface.

This involves widening the existing road pavement to accommodate more lanes to ease traffic congestion, improve traffic flow, and increase road capacity. Road widening is essential in high-traffic areas where there is a need to increase the capacity of the national road network.
This involves improving the quality of the road's off-carriageway, such as the shoulder, median, and roadside, to enhance road safety and improve the comfort of road users.
This involves the construction of a new pavement surface on unpaved national roads to improve road quality, increase national road capacity, and enhance the safety and comfort of road users.
